reason: The cited lines show the tool executes the provided SQL through a connector and returns result sets/messages in the tool response. That supports SECRET because database result sets reached through a configured connector may contain non-public database data returned to the agent. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution, so HOSTEXEC is not supported. They do not establish delivery of data to an attacker-readable destination; SQL execution might have write effects depending on configuration/SQL/database, but the cited lines alone do not show an attacker-readable sink. They also do not establish that returned result sets/messages are attacker-controllable; database contents could be untrusted in some deployments, but that is not settled by these lines alone.
